approachQuestion.prompt:
Cable contact test

Given integer points A,B,P, return whether P lies on the closed segment from A to B. Endpoints count; A and B may coincide.

Example 1: A=(0,0),B=(4,2),P=(2,1) -> true.
Example 2: A=(0,0),B=(4,2),P=(6,3) -> false.
Example 3: A=B=(2,2),P=(2,3) -> false.

Constraints and assumptions: Coordinates are integers in [-10^6,10^6]. Return one boolean. Use exact signed 64-bit calculations, for all legal coordinates. Choose the best time bound among the offered correct methods, then the least auxiliary storage when time ties.

options.text: Require cross(B-A,P-A)=0 and both coordinates of P to be within the inclusive coordinate ranges of A,B.
options.feedback: The cross test selects the supporting line and the box selects its finite closed segment. For A=B the box contains only that point.
On the line, the two vectors from the endpoints point in opposite directions exactly within the closed segment. If A=B the dot is a squared distance and is nonpositive only at A.
A=(0,0),B=(4,2),P=(6,3) is collinear but beyond the segment.

options.text: Return true exactly when P lies inside the endpoints' inclusive bounding box.
options.feedback: A=(0,0),B=(2,2),P=(1,0) is inside the box but off the line.

feedback.reason: Combine exact collinearity with finite segment bounds, including a point segment.
details: Compute cross(B-A,P-A). Require it to be zero and require P.x and P.y to lie in their respective inclusive endpoint ranges. These checks also handle A=B.

Collinearity alone accepts points beyond the segment. Combine zero cross product with both inclusive coordinate bounds. For coincident endpoints the box collapses to that one point, correctly handling a degenerate segment.

“Require cross(B-A,P-A)=0 and both coordinates of P to be within the inclusive coordinate ranges of A,B.”: The cross test selects the supporting line and the box selects its finite closed segment. For A=B the box contains only that point.

“Require cross(B-A,P-A)=0 and dot(P-A,P-B)<=0.”: On the line, the two vectors from the endpoints point in opposite directions exactly within the closed segment. If A=B the dot is a squared distance and is nonpositive only at A.
“Return true exactly when cross(B-A,P-A)=0.”: A=(0,0),B=(4,2),P=(6,3) is collinear but beyond the segment.
“Return true exactly when P lies inside the endpoints' inclusive bounding box.”: A=(0,0),B=(2,2),P=(1,0) is inside the box but off the line.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (cross-and-box). Let C be the largest absolute coordinate magnitude; all numbers fit the stated word model. Choose its tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
Include initialization and any copying; no hidden preprocessing or cache.

feedback.reason: A fixed cross-and-box test uses constant arithmetic and storage.
details: The analyzed cross-and-box method uses a fixed number of differences, products and comparisons for three points. Coordinate magnitude changes values, not the number of fixed-width operations. No list, stack or traversal is needed; cross and dot magnitudes are bounded by 8*10^12.
Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Correct: a fixed number of exact tests on three points.
“O(C) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This would enumerate coordinate positions, which the method avoids.
“O(log(C + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The method performs no coordinate-dependent loop.
“O(1) time, O(C + 1) auxiliary space”: It allocates no table indexed by coordinates.
